title: FAA Orders Nationwide Ground Stop: All Departing Flights Grounded, Including Laredo
excerpt: The FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop on Friday afternoon, Nov. 13, holding all departing flights across the United States — including departures from Laredo International Airport — until further notice.
content:
The Federal Aviation Administration ordered a nationwide ground stop on Friday afternoon, Nov. 13, holding all departing flights across the United States on the ground until further notice — including departures from Laredo International Airport.

The order, issued by the FAA's Air Traffic Control System Command Center, took effect at 2:54 p.m. Central Time. In its advisory, the FAA said all airports were ground stopped "due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety."

An FAA spokesperson said a communications problem is affecting Air Route Traffic Control Centers, which handle flights traveling across the country. U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the ground stop followed a communication issue impacting all air traffic control centers, and that FAA technicians are investigating.

Flights already in the air are not being ordered to land immediately and will continue to their destinations. Inbound international flights will be handled on a case-by-case basis, according to the advisory.

The advisory lists an effective period running through 11:30 p.m. Eastern Time on Friday, but the FAA said departing traffic should remain grounded until further notice and has not given an estimate for when normal operations will return.

The last nationwide ground stop came in January 2023, when a pilot notification system failed. Before that, the last one was after the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks.

Travelers flying out of Laredo International Airport should check their flight status with their airline before heading to the airport, as delays are expected nationwide. This is a developing story.

Source: Federal Aviation Administration advisory, Nov. 13, 2026, as reported by USA Today, CNN and Reuters; flagged by Hammrod News Laredo TX.
